docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This guide covers all the ways to install SecretZero and its optional dependencies.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python: 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12
  • Operating System: Linux, macOS, or Windows
  • pip: Latest version recommended

docs.title: Basic Installation
docs.text:
The simplest way to install SecretZero:

pip install secretzero

This installs the core functionality including:

  • CLI commands
  • Configuration parsing and validation
  • Local file storage support
  • Basic secret generators

docs.title: Optional Dependencies
docs.text: SecretZero uses optional dependencies for cloud providers and additional features. Install only what you need:

docs.title: Cloud Providers
docs.text:
AWSAzureHashiCorp VaultAll Cloud Providers 
pip install secretzero[aws]

Includes:

  • AWS Secrets Manager support
  • SSM Parameter Store support
  • IAM role authentication
  • boto3 SDK
pip install secretzero[azure]

Includes:

  • Azure Key Vault support
  • Managed Identity authentication
  • Azure SDK
pip install secretzero[vault]

Includes:

  • Vault KV v2 support
  • Token and AppRole authentication
  • hvac client library
pip install secretzero[aws,azure,vault]

docs.title: CI/CD Platforms
docs.text:
GitHubGitLabJenkinsAll CI/CD 
pip install secretzero[github]

Includes:

  • GitHub Actions secrets
  • Repository, environment, and organization secrets
  • PyGithub library
pip install secretzero[gitlab]

Includes:

  • GitLab CI/CD variables
  • Project and group variables
  • python-gitlab library
pip install secretzero[jenkins]

Includes:

  • Jenkins credentials
  • String and username/password credentials
  • python-jenkins library
pip install secretzero[cicd]

docs.title: Container Platforms
docs.text:
pip install secretzero[kubernetes]

Includes:

  • Kubernetes Secret support
  • External Secrets Operator integration
  • All secret types (TLS, Docker, SSH, etc.)
  • Official Kubernetes Python client

docs.title: API Server
docs.text:
pip install secretzero[api]

Includes:

  • FastAPI web framework
  • Uvicorn ASGI server
  • OpenAPI documentation
  • REST API endpoints

docs.title: Documentation Tools
docs.text:
pip install secretzero[docs]

Includes:

  • MkDocs with Material theme
  • Documentation generation tools
  • API documentation plugins

docs.title: Everything
docs.text:
Install all optional dependencies:

pip install secretzero[all]

This includes all cloud providers, CI/CD platforms, Kubernetes support, API server, and documentation tools.

docs.title: Development Installation
docs.text: For contributing to SecretZero:

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/zloeber/SecretZero.git
cd SecretZero

docs.title: 2. Create a Virtual Environment
docs.text:
Linux/macOSWindows 
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate

docs.title: 3. Install in Development Mode
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[all,dev]"

This installs:

  • All optional dependencies
  • Development tools (pytest, black, ruff, mypy)
  • The package in editable mode

docs.title: 4. Verify Installation
docs.text:
secretzero --version
pytest

docs.title: Using pipx
docs.text:
pipx installs Python applications in isolated environments:

pipx install secretzero
pipx inject secretzero boto3 azure-identity  # Add optional dependencies

docs.title: Using Poetry
docs.text:
If you use Poetry for dependency management:

poetry add secretzero
poetry add secretzero[aws,azure,vault]

docs.title: Using Docker
docs.text:
You can run SecretZero in a Docker container:

FROM python:3.11-slim

# Install SecretZero
RUN pip install secretzero[all]

# Copy your Secretfile
COPY Secretfile.yml /app/Secretfile.yml
WORKDIR /app

# Run SecretZero
CMD ["secretzero", "sync"]

Build and run:

docker build -t secretzero .
docker run -v $(pwd):/app secretzero

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text: After installation, verify everything is working:

docs.title: 1. Check Version
docs.text:
secretzero --version

Expected output: 

SecretZero version 0.1.0

docs.title: 2. Check Available Commands
docs.text:
secretzero --help

You should see all available commands: - create - Create new Secretfile - validate - Validate configuration - sync - Generate and sync secrets - show - Show secret status - rotate - Rotate secrets - policy - Check policies - drift - Detect drift - test - Test connectivity

docs.title: 3. Test Installation
docs.text:
Create a test Secretfile:

secretzero create

This creates a Secretfile.yml with example configuration.

Validate it:

secretzero validate

If you see ✅ messages, everything is installed correctly!

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
To upgrade to the latest version:

pip install --upgrade secretzero

To upgrade with all dependencies:

pip install --upgrade secretzero[all]

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
To remove SecretZero:

pip uninstall secretzero

This removes the package but leaves your configuration files intact.

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
If you get a Python version error:

# Check your Python version
python --version

# Use a specific Python version
python3.11 -m pip install secretzero

docs.title: Permission Errors
docs.text:
If you get permission errors on Linux/macOS:

pip install --user secretzero

Or use a virtual environment (recommended):

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install secretzero

docs.title: Import Errors
docs.text:
If you get import errors after installation:

# Ensure you're using the correct Python/pip
which python
which pip

docs.title: Cloud Provider Dependencies
docs.text:
If cloud provider commands fail:

pip show boto3          # AWS
pip show azure-identity # Azure
pip show hvac           # Vault

pip install secretzero[aws,azure,vault]

docs.text:
On macOS with Apple Silicon (M1/M2):

xcode-select --install

  1. Download Visual C++ Build Tools

  3. Then install SecretZero

Ubuntu/DebianCentOS/RHELAlpine 
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install python3-dev python3-pip
pip install secretzero

pip install secretzero

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get started with SecretZero in 5 minutes! This guide will walk you through creating your first secret.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Make sure you have SecretZero installed:

pip install secretzero

See the Installation Guide for more options.

docs.title: Step 1: Initialize a Project
docs.text:
Create a new Secretfile in your project directory:

secretzero create

This creates a Secretfile.yml with example configuration:

version: "1.0"
metadata:
  name: my-project
  description: My first SecretZero project

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

docs.title: Step 2: Validate Configuration
docs.text:
Validate your Secretfile:

secretzero validate

Expected output:

✓ Configuration is valid
✓ Found 1 secret(s)
✓ Found 1 target(s)

docs.title: Step 3: Preview Secret Generation
docs.text:
See what would be generated without making changes:

secretzero sync --dry-run

Expected output:

[Dry Run] Would generate secret: api_key
  ✓ Would generate field: value (random-string, length=32)
  ✓ Would write to: .env (dotenv format)

[Dry Run] Summary:
  Secrets to generate: 1
  Secrets to skip: 0
  Targets to update: 1

docs.title: Step 4: Generate the Secret
docs.text:
Generate and sync the secret:

secretzero sync

Expected output:

✓ Generated secret: api_key
  ✓ Generated field: value
  ✓ Wrote to: .env

✓ Updated lockfile: .gitsecrets.lock

Summary:
  Generated: 1
  Skipped: 0
  Failed: 0

docs.title: Step 5: Verify the Results
docs.text:
Check the generated secret in your .env file:

cat .env

Output:

API_KEY=abcd1234efgh5678ijkl9012mnop3456

Check the lockfile:

cat .gitsecrets.lock

The lockfile contains hashed values and metadata:

{
  "version": "1.0",
  "secrets": {
    "api_key": {
      "fields": {
        "value": {
          "hash": "sha256:a1b2c3d4...",
          "generated_at": "2026-02-16T12:00:00Z",
          "algorithm": "random-string"
        }
      },
      "targets": [".env"],
      "last_modified": "2026-02-16T12:00:00Z"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Step 6: View Secret Status
docs.text:
Check the status of your secret:

secretzero show api_key

Output:

Secret: api_key
Type: api_key
Status: ✓ Generated

Fields:
  value:
    Algorithm: random-string
    Generated: 2026-02-16 12:00:00 UTC
    Hash: sha256:a1b2c3d4...

Last Modified: 2026-02-16 12:00:00 UTC

docs.title: 🎉 Congratulations!
docs.text:
You've successfully:

✅ Created a Secretfile ✅ Validated the configuration ✅ Generated a secret ✅ Synced it to a local file ✅ Tracked it in a lockfile

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text: Now that you understand the basics, explore more features:

docs.title: Add More Secrets
docs.text:
Edit your Secretfile.yml to add more secrets:

secrets:
  api_key:
    # ... existing configuration ...

  database_password:
    template:
      type: password
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-password
            length: 32
            include_symbols: true
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

Then sync again:

secretzero sync

docs.title: Use Different Targets
docs.text:
Store secrets in multiple locations:

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv
      - type: local-file
        path: config.json
        format: json
      - type: local-file
        path: config.yml
        format: yaml

docs.title: Add Cloud Providers
docs.text:
Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager:

providers:
  aws:
    type: aws
    auth:
      type: ambient  # Uses IAM roles/profiles

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    targets:
      - type: aws-secretsmanager
        provider: aws
        name: /prod/api_key
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

First install AWS support:

pip install secretzero[aws]

Then sync:

secretzero sync

docs.title: Test Provider Connectivity
docs.text:
Before syncing to cloud providers, test connectivity:

secretzero test

This verifies that:

  • Provider authentication is working
  • Required permissions are available
  • Network connectivity is OK

docs.title: Add Rotation Policies
docs.text:
Automatically rotate secrets based on time:

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    rotation:
      period: 90d  # Rotate every 90 days
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

Check rotation status:

secretzero rotate --dry-run

Execute rotation:

secretzero rotate

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text: Here are some quick examples for common scenarios:

docs.title: Database Credentials
docs.text:
secrets:
  db_password:
    template:
      type: database
      fields:
        - name: username
          generator:
            type: static
            value: myapp_user
        - name: password
          generator:
            type: random-password
            length: 32
        - name: host
          generator:
            type: static
            value: db.example.com
        - name: port
          generator:
            type: static
            value: "5432"
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

docs.title: API Tokens
docs.text:
secrets:
  github_token:
    template:
      type: token
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 40
            charset: hex
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv
        key: GITHUB_TOKEN

docs.title: Multi-Field Secrets
docs.text:
secrets:
  oauth_credentials:
    template:
      type: oauth
      fields:
        - name: client_id
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
        - name: client_secret
          generator:
            type: random-password
            length: 64
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: oauth.json
        format: json

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
Use Dry Run First

Always use --dry-run to preview changes before applying them: 

secretzero sync --dry-run

Protect Your Secrets

Add secret files to .gitignore: 

.env
.env.local
.gitsecrets.lock

Environment Variables

You can override generated values with environment variables: 

export API_KEY_VALUE="my-existing-key"
secretzero sync  # Will use the environment variable

Lockfile Benefits

The lockfile (.gitsecrets.lock):

  • Tracks secret history
  • Prevents unnecessary regeneration
  • Enables drift detection
  • Supports compliance audits

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This document provides a deep dive into SecretZero's architecture, design decisions, and extensibility points.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SecretZero follows a layered, modular architecture designed for extensibility, testability, and maintainability.

graph TB
    A[User Interface Layer] --> B[Engine Layer]
    B --> C[Provider Layer]
    B --> D[Generator Layer]
    B --> E[Policy Layer]
    C --> F[Target Layer]
    D --> F
    F --> G[Storage Layer]
    B --> H[Lockfile Layer]

    A1[CLI] --> A
    A2[API] --> A

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#fff4e6
    style C fill:#f3e5f5
    style D fill:#f3e5f5
    style E fill:#f3e5f5
    style F fill:#e8f5e9
    style G fill:#ffebee
    style H fill:#fce4ec

docs.title: 1. User Interface Layer
docs.text: Provides interfaces for interacting with SecretZero.

docs.text:
Location: src/secretzero/cli.py

Responsibilities: - Parse command-line arguments - Validate user input - Display formatted output - Handle user interactions

Key Commands:

docs.text:

docs.title: 2. Engine Layer
docs.text:
Core business logic for secret management operations.

graph LR
    A[Engine Layer] --> B[Sync Engine]
    A --> C[Rotation Engine]
    A --> D[Policy Engine]
    A --> E[Drift Detector]
    A --> F[Config Loader]

docs.title: Sync Engine
docs.text:
Location: src/secretzero/sync.py

Responsibilities: - Orchestrate secret generation - Manage provider initialization - Store secrets in targets - Update lockfile

Algorithm:

FOR EACH secret IN secretfile:
    IF secret.one_time AND exists_in_lockfile(secret):
        SKIP
    ELSE:
        value = generate_secret(secret)
        FOR EACH target IN secret.targets:
            store_secret(target, value)
        update_lockfile(secret, value)

Key Methods:

class SyncEngine:
    def sync(self, secretfile: Secretfile, lockfile: Lockfile) -> SyncResult:
        """Sync all secrets"""
        pass

    def _generate_secret(self, secret: Secret) -> str:
        """Generate secret value"""
        pass

    def _store_in_target(self, target: Target, value: str) -> None:
        """Store secret in target"""
        pass

docs.title: Rotation Engine
docs.text:
Location: src/secretzero/rotation.py

Responsibilities: - Calculate rotation due dates - Determine which secrets need rotation - Execute rotation operations - Update rotation metadata

Algorithm:

FOR EACH secret IN secretfile:
    IF NOT secret.rotation_period:
        SKIP
    IF secret.one_time:
        WARN (one_time secrets don't rotate)
    ELSE:
        due_date = last_rotated + rotation_period
        IF current_date >= due_date OR force:
            rotate_secret(secret)
            update_rotation_metadata(secret)

Key Methods:

class RotationEngine:
    def check_rotation_status(self, secretfile: Secretfile, lockfile: Lockfile) -> List[RotationStatus]:
        """Check which secrets need rotation"""
        pass

    def execute_rotation(self, secrets: List[str]) -> RotationResult:
        """Rotate specified secrets"""
        pass

    def _calculate_due_date(self, secret: Secret, lockfile: Lockfile) -> datetime:
        """Calculate when rotation is due"""
        pass

docs.title: Policy Engine
docs.text:
Location: src/secretzero/policy.py

Responsibilities: - Validate secrets against policies - Enforce compliance requirements - Generate violation reports - Provide remediation suggestions

Policy Types:

class RotationPolicy:
    """Enforce rotation requirements"""
    require_rotation_period: bool
    max_age: timedelta
    severity: Severity

class CompliancePolicy:
    """Enforce compliance standards"""
    standard: str  # soc2, iso27001
    severity: Severity

class AccessPolicy:
    """Control target access"""
    allowed_targets: List[str]
    denied_targets: List[str]
    severity: Severity

docs.title: Drift Detector
docs.text:
Location: src/secretzero/drift.py

Responsibilities: - Compare lockfile with actual state - Detect unauthorized changes - Identify missing secrets - Report drift status

Detection Algorithm:

FOR EACH secret IN lockfile:
    FOR EACH target IN secret.targets:
        actual_value = read_target(target)
        expected_hash = lockfile.hash(secret)
        IF hash(actual_value) != expected_hash:
            REPORT drift(secret, target)

docs.text:

docs.title: 3. Provider Layer
docs.text:
Manages authentication and connectivity to secret storage backends.

docs.text:
Random Password (src/secretzero/generators/random_password.py):

class RandomPasswordGenerator(BaseGenerator):
    def generate(self, config: dict) -> str:
        length = config.get('length', 32)
        charset = self._build_charset(config)
        return ''.join(secrets.choice(charset) for _ in range(length))

Random String (src/secretzero/generators/random_string.py):

class RandomStringGenerator(BaseGenerator):
    def generate(self, config: dict) -> str:
        length = config.get('length', 32)
        charset_name = config.get('charset', 'alphanumeric')
        charset = self._get_charset(charset_name)
        return ''.join(secrets.choice(charset) for _ in range(length))

Static (src/secretzero/generators/static.py):

class StaticGenerator(BaseGenerator):
    def generate(self, config: dict) -> str:
        value = config.get('value', config.get('default', ''))
        validation = config.get('validation')
        if validation and not re.match(validation, value):
            raise ValueError(f"Value doesn't match pattern: {validation}")
        return value

Script (src/secretzero/generators/script.py):

class ScriptGenerator(BaseGenerator):
    def generate(self, config: dict) -> str:
        command = config['command']
        args = config.get('args', [])
        timeout = config.get('timeout', 30)
        result = subprocess.run(
            [command] + args,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout
        )
        return result.stdout.strip()

class FileTarget(BaseTarget):

        if format == 'dotenv':

            self._store_yaml(secret_name, value)

AWS Secrets Manager (src/secretzero/targets/aws.py):

class SecretsManagerTarget(BaseTarget):
    def store(self, secret_name: str, value: str) -> None:
        client = self.provider.get_client('secretsmanager')
        try:
            client.create_secret(
                Name=self.config['name'],
                SecretString=value
            )
        except client.exceptions.ResourceExistsException:
            client.put_secret_value(
                SecretId=self.config['name'],
                SecretString=value
            )

docs.title: Secret Generation Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI
    participant Sync Engine
    participant Generator
    participant Target
    participant Lockfile

    User->>CLI: secretzero sync
    CLI->>Sync Engine: sync(secretfile, lockfile)

    loop For each secret
        Sync Engine->>Lockfile: check if exists
        alt One-time and exists
            Lockfile-->>Sync Engine: Skip
        else Generate
            Sync Engine->>Generator: generate(config)
            Generator-->>Sync Engine: value

            loop For each target
                Sync Engine->>Target: store(name, value)
                Target-->>Sync Engine: Success
            end

            Sync Engine->>Lockfile: update(secret, hash)
        end
    end

    Sync Engine->>Lockfile: save()
    Sync Engine-->>CLI: Result
    CLI-->>User: Display summary

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI
    participant Rotation Engine
    participant Lockfile
    participant Sync Engine

    CLI->>Rotation Engine: check_status()

docs.title: Secret Handling
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Generation] --> B[In-Memory]
    B --> C[Hashing]
    C --> D[Lockfile - Hash Only]
    B --> E[Encryption]
    E --> F[Transmission]
    F --> G[Storage]

    style B fill:#ffebee
    style D fill:#e8f5e9
    style E fill:#e1f5ff
    style G fill:#fff4e6

Principles:

  1. Minimal Exposure: Secrets exist in memory only during operations
  2. One-Way Hashing: Lockfile stores SHA-256 hashes, not values
  3. Encryption in Transit: All cloud API calls over HTTPS
  4. Encryption at Rest: Cloud providers handle storage encryption
  5. No Logging: Secret values never logged

def verify_api_key(provided_key: str, expected_key: str) -> bool:
    # Timing-safe comparison

    expected_hash = hashlib.sha256(expected_key.encode()).digest()
    return secrets.compare_digest(provided_hash, expected_hash)

class AuditLogger:

    def notify(self, event: AuditEvent) -> None:
        for observer in self._observers:

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: Common questions about SecretZero installation, configuration, usage, and troubleshooting.

docs.title: What is SecretZero?
docs.text: SecretZero is a secrets management tool that automates the creation, seeding, and lifecycle management of project secrets through a declarative, schema-driven workflow. Think of it as "Terraform for secrets" - you declare what secrets you need, and SecretZero handles generation, storage, rotation, and compliance.

docs.title: Why should I use SecretZero?
docs.text:
Use SecretZero if you need to:

  • Bootstrap new environments from scratch without manual secret handling
  • Track all secrets in your project in a single source of truth
  • Automate rotation of secrets based on compliance policies
  • Synchronize secrets across multiple platforms (AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, etc.)
  • Document your project's secrets surface area
  • Enforce compliance with SOC2, ISO27001, or custom policies

docs.title: How is SecretZero different from other tools?
docs.text:
Feature SecretZero HashiCorp Vault AWS Secrets Manager 1Password/Bitwarden Declarative Config ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ Multi-Provider ✅ ❌ ❌ Partial Secret Generation ✅ Partial ❌ ❌ Rotation Policies ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ Lockfile Tracking ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ CI/CD Integration ✅ Partial Partial Partial Local Development ✅ Partial ❌ ✅

Key Differences:

  • Vault: Runtime secret storage; SecretZero: Lifecycle management
  • AWS Secrets Manager: AWS-only; SecretZero: Multi-cloud
  • 1Password: Human-oriented; SecretZero: Automation-oriented

docs.title: Is SecretZero production-ready?
docs.text:
Yes! SecretZero has:

  • ✅ 200+ tests with high code coverage
  • ✅ Zero security vulnerabilities (CodeQL verified)
  • ✅ Battle-tested across 7 development phases
  • ✅ SOC2/ISO27001 compliance support
  • ✅ Comprehensive documentation

docs.title: Is SecretZero open source?
docs.text:
Yes, SecretZero is open source under the Apache 2.0 license. You can:

  • Use it commercially
  • Modify and distribute
  • Contribute improvements
  • View the source code

See LICENSE for details.

docs.title: What are the system requirements?
docs.text:
• Python: 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, or 3.12
  • Operating System: Linux, macOS, or Windows
  • pip: Latest version recommended

Optional dependencies based on providers you use.

docs.title: How do I install SecretZero?
docs.text:
Basic installation:

pip install secretzero

With specific providers:

# AWS support
pip install secretzero[aws]

# All providers
pip install secretzero[all]

See the Installation Guide for details.

docs.title: Do I need cloud accounts to use SecretZero?
docs.text:
No! SecretZero works perfectly for local development:

targets:
  - type: local-file
    path: .env
    format: dotenv

Cloud providers are optional and only needed if you want to store secrets in AWS, Azure, etc.

docs.title: How do I upgrade SecretZero?
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade secretzero

With all dependencies:

pip install --upgrade secretzero[all]

SecretZero maintains backward compatibility with existing Secretfile.yml and lockfiles.

docs.title: Can I use SecretZero in Docker?
docs.text:
Yes! Example Dockerfile:

FROM python:3.11-slim

# Install SecretZero
RUN pip install secretzero[all]

# Copy configuration
COPY Secretfile.yml /app/
WORKDIR /app

# Run SecretZero
CMD ["secretzero", "sync"]

Build and run:

docker build -t secretzero .
docker run -v $(pwd):/app secretzero

docs.title: How do I create a Secretfile?
docs.text:
Initialize with a template:

secretzero create

Or create manually:

version: "1.0"

metadata:
  name: my-project

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

See First Project for a complete walkthrough.

docs.title: Can I use environment variables in the Secretfile?
docs.text:
Yes! Use Jinja2 templating:

variables:
  environment: "{{env.ENVIRONMENT or 'development'}}"
  region: "{{env.AWS_REGION or 'us-east-1'}}"

secrets:
  api_key:
    targets:
      - type: aws-secretsmanager
        name: "/{{var.environment}}/api_key"
        region: "{{var.region}}"

docs.title: How do I manage secrets for multiple environments?
docs.text:
Option 1: Variables

variables:
  environment: "{{env.ENVIRONMENT}}"

secrets:
  api_key:
    targets:
      - type: aws-secretsmanager
        name: "/{{var.environment}}/api_key"

ENVIRONMENT=production secretzero sync
ENVIRONMENT=staging secretzero sync

Option 2: Separate Lockfiles

secretzero sync --lockfile .gitsecrets-prod.lock
secretzero sync --lockfile .gitsecrets-staging.lock

Option 3: Separate Secretfiles

secretzero sync --file Secretfile-prod.yml
secretzero sync --file Secretfile-staging.yml

docs.title: Can I use existing secrets instead of generating new ones?
docs.text:
Yes! Set environment variables matching the secret name:

export API_KEY="my-existing-key"
secretzero sync

SecretZero checks environment variables first before generating.

docs.title: How do I validate my Secretfile?
docs.text:
secretzero validate

This checks:

  • ✅ YAML syntax
  • ✅ Required fields
  • ✅ Type validation
  • ✅ Provider configuration
  • ✅ Generator configuration

docs.title: Which cloud providers are supported?
docs.text:
• AWS: Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store
  • Azure: Key Vault
  • HashiCorp Vault: KV v1 & v2
  • GitHub Actions: Repository, environment, and organization secrets
  • GitLab CI/CD: Project and group variables
  • Jenkins: String and username/password credentials
  • Kubernetes: Native Secrets and External Secrets Operator

docs.title: How do I authenticate with AWS?
docs.text:
SecretZero uses standard AWS credential chain:

providers:
  aws:
    kind: aws
    auth:
      kind: ambient  # Uses default credential chain
      config:
        region: us-east-1

Supported methods:

  1. Environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
  2. AWS credentials file (~/.aws/credentials)
  3. IAM roles (EC2 instance profiles, ECS task roles)
  4. AWS profiles
export AWS_PROFILE=myprofile
secretzero sync

docs.title: How do I authenticate with Azure?
docs.text:
providers:
  azure:
    kind: azure
    auth:
      kind: default  # Uses Azure credential chain

Supported methods:

  1. Environment variables
  2. Managed Identity (in Azure VMs/containers)
  3. Azure CLI (az login)
  4. Visual Studio Code credentials

docs.title: How do I test provider connectivity?
docs.text:
secretzero test

This verifies:

  • ✅ Authentication is working
  • ✅ Network connectivity
  • ✅ Required permissions
  • ✅ Provider configuration

docs.title: What AWS permissions does SecretZero need?
docs.text:
For Secrets Manager:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "secretsmanager:CreateSecret",
        "secretsmanager:UpdateSecret",
        "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret",
        "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:/myapp/*"
    }
  ]
}

For SSM Parameter Store:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ssm:PutParameter",
        "ssm:GetParameter",
        "ssm:DescribeParameters"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/myapp/*"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: What types of secrets can SecretZero generate?
docs.text:
• Random Passwords: Cryptographically secure passwords
  • Random Strings: Alphanumeric tokens, hex strings, etc.
  • Static Values: Usernames, URLs, configuration values
  • Script-Generated: SSH keys, certificates, custom values
  • API-Generated: Fetch from external APIs (planned)

docs.title: How secure are generated passwords?
docs.text:
Very secure! SecretZero uses:

  • Python's secrets module (cryptographically secure)
  • System entropy sources
  • Configurable length (default: 32 characters)
  • Customizable character sets

Generated passwords have high entropy (e.g., 32 chars = ~192 bits of entropy with full character set).

docs.title: Can I customize password requirements?
docs.text:
Yes! Full control over character sets:

generator:
  type: random-password
  length: 32
  include_upper: true
  include_lower: true
  include_numbers: true
  include_symbols: true
  exclude_characters: '"@/\`'  # Exclude problematic chars

docs.title: How do I generate SSH keys?
docs.text:
Use the script generator:

generator:
  type: script
  command: ssh-keygen
  args:
    - -t
    - rsa
    - -b
    - "4096"
    - -f
    - /dev/stdout
    - -N
    - ""

Or use dedicated tools like ssh-keygen directly and import the keys as static values.

docs.title: Can I use external APIs to generate secrets?
docs.text:
Not directly in current version, but you can use the script generator to call APIs:

generator:
  type: script
  command: curl
  args:
    - -s
    - https://api.example.com/generate-key

Native API generator support is planned for future releases.

docs.title: Where can I store secrets?
docs.text:
Local Storage:

  • .env files (dotenv format)
  • JSON files
  • YAML files
  • TOML files

Cloud Storage:

  • AWS Secrets Manager
  • AWS SSM Parameter Store
  • Azure Key Vault
  • HashiCorp Vault

CI/CD Platforms:

  • GitHub Actions Secrets
  • GitLab CI/CD Variables
  • Jenkins Credentials

Container Platforms:

  • Kubernetes Secrets
  • External Secrets Operator

docs.title: Can I store the same secret in multiple locations?
docs.text:
Yes! That's a core feature:

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
      - type: aws-secretsmanager
        name: /myapp/api_key
      - type: kubernetes-secret
        namespace: production

The same value is stored in all targets.

docs.title: What happens if one target fails?
docs.text:
SecretZero continues with other targets and reports errors at the end:

✓ Generated secret: api_key
  ✓ Wrote to: .env
  ✗ Failed to write to: AWS Secrets Manager (No credentials)
  ✓ Wrote to: Kubernetes

Summary:
  Generated: 1
  Targets Updated: 2
  Targets Failed: 1

The lockfile is still updated for successful targets.

docs.title: How do I update an existing secret?
docs.text:
Option 1: Force Sync

secretzero sync --force

Option 2: Rotate

secretzero rotate api_key --force

Option 3: Change Configuration

Modify the generator config in Secretfile.yml, then:

secretzero sync

docs.title: How does secret rotation work?
docs.text:
1. Define rotation period: 

    rotation:
  period: 90d

  2. Check rotation status: 

    secretzero rotate --dry-run

  3. Rotate due secrets: 

    secretzero rotate

The lockfile tracks last_rotated timestamp and rotation_count.

docs.title: What rotation periods are supported?
docs.text:
• Days: 7d, 30d, 90d
  • Weeks: 1w, 2w, 4w
  • Months: 1m, 3m, 6m
  • Years: 1y, 2y

docs.title: Can I prevent a secret from being rotated?
docs.text:
Yes! Use one_time: true:

secrets:
  master_key:
    one_time: true

This generates the secret once and never rotates it automatically.

docs.title: How do I enforce SOC2 compliance?
docs.text:
Add SOC2 to metadata:

metadata:
  compliance:
    - soc2

SecretZero automatically checks:

  • ✅ All secrets have rotation periods
  • ✅ Rotation periods ≤ 90 days
  • ✅ Secrets are tracked in lockfile

Verify compliance:

secretzero policy

docs.title: What's the difference between rotation and regeneration?
docs.text:
Rotation:

  • Scheduled based on time period
  • Updates last_rotated timestamp
  • Increments rotation_count
  • Respects one_time flag

Regeneration (force sync):

  • Manual operation
  • Ignores rotation schedule
  • Doesn't update rotation metadata
  • Ignores one_time flag with --force

docs.title: What is the lockfile?
docs.text:
The lockfile (.gitsecrets.lock) tracks secret state:

  • SHA-256 hashes of secret values
  • Creation and update timestamps
  • Rotation history
  • Target information

It does NOT contain actual secret values.

docs.title: Is it safe to commit the lockfile?
docs.text:
Yes! The lockfile contains only:

  • One-way SHA-256 hashes
  • Timestamps
  • Metadata

No actual secret values are stored. Committing it enables:

  • ✅ Drift detection
  • ✅ Audit trails
  • ✅ Team synchronization

docs.title: What if I lose the lockfile?
docs.text:
No problem! Just regenerate:

secretzero sync

SecretZero will:

  1. Detect missing lockfile
  2. Generate new hashes for current secrets
  3. Create new lockfile

Note: You'll lose rotation history.

docs.title: Can I manually edit the lockfile?
docs.text:
Not recommended! The lockfile is auto-generated and managed by SecretZero. Manual edits may cause:

  • Incorrect drift detection
  • Failed validation
  • Sync issues

If you need to reset, just delete it and run secretzero sync.

docs.title: How do I use SecretZero in CI/CD?
docs.text:
GitHub Actions Example:

name: Sync Secrets

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  sync:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Install SecretZero
        run: pip install secretzero[aws]

      - name: Sync Secrets
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
        run: secretzero sync

GitLab CI Example:

sync-secrets:
  image: python:3.11
  script:
    - pip install secretzero[aws]
    - secretzero sync
  variables:
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: $AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

docs.title: How do I enforce policies in CI/CD?
docs.text:
Add a policy check step:

- name: Check Policies
  run: |
    secretzero policy --fail-on-warning

This fails the CI pipeline if any policy violations are found.

docs.title: Can SecretZero read secrets from CI/CD platforms?
docs.text:
SecretZero primarily writes secrets to CI/CD platforms (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins).

For reading, use the native tools:

  • GitHub: ${{ secrets.SECRET_NAME }}
  • GitLab: $SECRET_NAME
  • Jenkins: credentials('secret-id')

docs.title: How do I rotate secrets automatically in CI/CD?
docs.text:
Scheduled GitHub Action:

name: Rotate Secrets

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * 0'  # Weekly

jobs:
  rotate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install SecretZero
        run: pip install secretzero[all]
      - name: Rotate Secrets
        run: secretzero rotate

docs.title: How do I start the API server?
docs.text:
# Generate API key
export SECRETZERO_API_KEY=$(python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))")

# Start server
secretzero-api

Access at http://localhost:8000

docs.title: What endpoints are available?
docs.text:
• GET / - API information
  • GET /health - Health check
  • POST /config/validate - Validate Secretfile
  • GET /secrets - List secrets
  • GET /secrets/{name}/status - Get secret status
  • POST /sync - Sync secrets
  • POST /rotation/check - Check rotation
  • POST /rotation/execute - Execute rotation
  • POST /policy/check - Check policies
  • POST /drift/check - Detect drift
  • GET /audit/logs - Get audit logs

See the API Getting Started Guide for details.

docs.title: How do I authenticate API requests?
docs.text:
Use the X-API-Key header:

curl -H "X-API-Key: $SECRETZERO_API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:8000/secrets

docs.title: Can I deploy the API in production?
docs.text:
Yes! Recommendations:

  1. Use HTTPS: Deploy behind reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik)
  2. Rotate API Keys: Regular key rotation
  3. Rate Limiting: Add rate limiting middleware
  4. Network Policies: Restrict access via firewall
  5. Monitoring: Add metrics and alerting

See production deployment guide in API documentation.

docs.text:
Cause: Package not installed or not in PATH

Solution:

# Verify installation
pip show secretzero

# Reinstall
pip install --force-reinstall secretzero

# Check PATH
which secretzero

docs.text:
Error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'boto3'

Cause: Optional dependencies not installed

Solution:

# Install AWS support
pip install secretzero[aws]

# Or install all providers
pip install secretzero[all]

docs.title: AWS authentication failed
docs.text:
Error: Unable to locate credentials

Solution:

# Check AWS credentials
aws sts get-caller-identity

# Set credentials
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-key
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1

# Or use AWS profile

docs.title: Secret not being generated
docs.text:
Issue: Secret shows as "skipped"

Possible Causes:

  1. One-time secret: Already exists in lockfile 

    secretzero show <secret-name>
# Use --force to regenerate
secretzero sync --force

  2. Environment variable set: Overriding generation 

    env | grep <SECRET_NAME>
# Unset to use generator
unset SECRET_NAME

docs.title: Lockfile conflicts
docs.text:
Error: Hash mismatch in lockfile

Solution:

# Check for drift
secretzero drift

# Force resync
secretzero sync --force

# Or regenerate lockfile
rm .gitsecrets.lock
secretzero sync

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: This guide helps you diagnose and resolve common issues with SecretZero. Issues are organized by category for easy navigation.

docs.title: Quick Diagnostics
docs.text:
Before diving into specific issues, run these commands to gather diagnostic information:

# Check SecretZero version
secretzero --version

# Validate configuration
secretzero validate

# Test provider connectivity
secretzero test

# Check Python version
python --version

# List installed packages
pip list | grep -E "(secretzero|boto3|azure|hvac)"

docs.title: Command Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom:

$ secretzero --version
bash: secretzero: command not found

Causes & Solutions:

docs.title: 1. Package Not Installed
docs.text:
# Install SecretZero
pip install secretzero

# Verify installation
pip show secretzero

docs.title: 2. Wrong Python/pip
docs.text:
# Check which Python/pip you're using
which python
which pip

# Use specific Python version
python3 -m pip install secretzero
python3 -m secretzero --version

docs.title: 3. Not in PATH
docs.text:
# Find installation location
pip show secretzero | grep Location

# Add to PATH (Linux/macOS)
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Or use full path
~/.local/bin/secretzero --version

docs.title: 4. Virtual Environment
docs.text:
# Activate virtual environment
source venv/bin/activate  # Linux/macOS
venv\Scripts\activate     # Windows

# Then install
pip install secretzero

docs.title: Import Errors
docs.text:
Symptom:

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'secretzero'

Solution:

# Reinstall with force
pip install --force-reinstall secretzero

# Or install in development mode
git clone https://github.com/zloeber/SecretZero.git
cd SecretZero
pip install -e .

docs.title: Dependency Conflicts
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR: pip's dependency resolver does not currently take into account all the packages...

Solution:

# Create clean virtual environment
python -m venv clean-venv
source clean-venv/bin/activate

# Install SecretZero
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install secretzero[all]

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR: Package 'secretzero' requires a different Python: 3.8.0 not in '>=3.9'

Solution:

# Check Python version
python --version

# Use Python 3.9+
python3.11 -m pip install secretzero
python3.11 -m secretzero --version

docs.title: Permission Errors
docs.text:
Symptom:

ERROR: Could not install packages due to an OSError: [Errno 13] Permission denied

Solution:

# Install for current user only
pip install --user secretzero

# Or use virtual environment (recommended)
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install secretzero

docs.title: Invalid YAML Syntax
docs.text:
Symptom:

$ secretzero validate
Error: YAML syntax error at line 15, column 3

Solution:

# Use YAML linter
pip install yamllint
yamllint Secretfile.yml

# Common issues:
# - Incorrect indentation (use 2 spaces, not tabs)
# - Missing colons
# - Unquoted special characters

Example Fix:

# ❌ Incorrect (tabs, missing quotes)
secrets:
    api_key:
        value: my-key-with-:-colon

# ✅ Correct (spaces, quoted)
secrets:
  api_key:
    value: "my-key-with-:-colon"

docs.title: Missing Required Fields
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: field required (type=value_error.missing)
  secrets -> 0 -> targets (field required)

Solution:

Every secret must have at least one target:

secrets:
  api_key:
    template:
      type: api_key
      fields:
        - name: value
          generator:
            type: random-string
            length: 32
    # ✅ Add target
    targets:
      - type: local-file
        path: .env
        format: dotenv

docs.title: Variable Interpolation Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Undefined variable 'var.environment'

Solution:

# ❌ Variable not defined
secrets:
  api_key:
    targets:
      - type: aws-secretsmanager
        name: "/{{var.environment}}/api_key"

# ✅ Define variable with default
variables:
  environment: "{{env.ENVIRONMENT or 'development'}}"

docs.title: Invalid Generator Configuration
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Invalid generator type 'random_pasword' (typo)

Solution:

# List valid generator types
secretzero secret-types

# Common typos:
# - random_pasword → random-password
# - random_str → random-string
# - stattic → static

docs.title: Invalid Target Configuration
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unknown target type 'aws_secrets_manager'

Solution:

# Check valid target types
secretzero secret-types

# Correct target type names:
# - aws-secretsmanager (not aws_secrets_manager)
# - aws-ssm-parameter (not aws_ssm_param)
# - local-file (not file)

docs.title: AWS Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unable to locate credentials. You can configure credentials by running "aws configure".

Diagnosis:

# Check AWS credentials
aws sts get-caller-identity

# Check environment variables
env | grep AWS

Solutions:

docs.title: Option 1: Environment Variables
docs.text:
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1

secretzero test

docs.title: Option 2: AWS Profile
docs.text:
export AWS_PROFILE=myprofile
secretzero test

docs.title: Option 3: AWS Configure
docs.text:
aws configure
secretzero test

docs.title: Option 4: IAM Role (EC2/ECS)
docs.text:
providers:
  aws:
    kind: aws
    auth:
      kind: ambient  # Uses IAM role automatically

docs.title: AWS Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the PutSecretValue operation

Solution:

Check IAM permissions:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "secretsmanager:CreateSecret",
        "secretsmanager:UpdateSecret",
        "secretsmanager:PutSecretValue",
        "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:/myapp/*"
    }
  ]
}

For SSM Parameter Store:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ssm:PutParameter",
        "ssm:GetParameter",
        "ssm:DescribeParameters"
      ],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:*:*:parameter/myapp/*"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Azure Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: DefaultAzureCredential failed to retrieve a token

Diagnosis:

# Check Azure CLI login
az account show

# Check environment variables
env | grep AZURE

Solutions:

docs.title: Option 1: Azure CLI
docs.text:
az login
secretzero test

docs.title: Option 2: Environment Variables
docs.text:
export AZURE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
export AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
export AZURE_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
secretzero test

docs.title: Option 3: Managed Identity (Azure VM/Container)
docs.text:
providers:
  azure:
    kind: azure
    auth:
      kind: managed_identity

docs.title: Vault Connection Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unable to connect to Vault at http://localhost:8200

Diagnosis:

# Check Vault is running
curl http://localhost:8200/v1/sys/health

# Check Vault token
echo $VAULT_TOKEN

Solutions:

# Start Vault (development mode)
vault server -dev

# Set token
export VAULT_TOKEN=root

# Or use custom URL
export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com
export VAULT_TOKEN=your-token

secretzero test

docs.title: Kubernetes Connection Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unable to connect to Kubernetes cluster

Diagnosis:

# Check kubectl connectivity
kubectl cluster-info

# Check kubeconfig
kubectl config view

Solutions:

# Set kubeconfig
export KUBECONFIG=/path/to/kubeconfig

# Or specify in Secretfile
providers:
  kubernetes:
    kind: kubernetes
    auth:
      kind: ambient
      config:
        kubeconfig: /path/to/kubeconfig
        context: production

docs.title: GitHub Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Bad credentials (401)

Solution:

# Generate Personal Access Token
# GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens

# Set token
export GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_your_token

secretzero test

Required Scopes:

  • repo (for repository secrets)
  • admin:org (for organization secrets)
  • workflow (for Actions secrets)

docs.title: GitLab Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: 401 Unauthorized

Solution:

# Generate Personal Access Token
# GitLab → Preferences → Access Tokens

# Set token
export GITLAB_TOKEN=glpat-your-token

secretzero test

Required Scopes:

  • api (full API access)
  • write_repository (for variables)

docs.title: Generator Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unknown generator type 'my-custom-generator'

Solution:

Use a supported generator type:

# List available generators
secretzero secret-types

# Supported generators:
# - random-password
# - random-string
# - static
# - script

docs.title: Script Generator Timeout
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Script generator timed out after 30 seconds

Solution:

Increase timeout:

generator:
  type: script
  command: long-running-command
  timeout: 120  # Increase to 120 seconds

docs.title: Script Generator Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Permission denied: 'my-script.sh'

Solution:

# Make script executable
chmod +x my-script.sh

# Or use interpreter explicitly
generator:
  type: script
  command: bash
  args:
    - my-script.sh

docs.title: Random Password Too Short
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Password length must be at least 8 characters

Solution:

generator:
  type: random-password
  length: 32  # Minimum 8, recommended 32+

docs.title: Static Generator Validation Failed
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Value 'my-value' does not match pattern '^[a-z]+$'

Solution:

# Option 1: Fix value to match pattern
generator:
  type: static
  value: myvalue  # Only lowercase letters

# Option 2: Update pattern
generator:
  type: static
  value: my-value
  validation: '^[a-z\-]+$'  # Allow hyphens

docs.title: Environment Variable Override Not Working
docs.text:
Symptom:

Secret still being generated even though environment variable is set.

Diagnosis:

# Check exact variable name format
# Format: {SECRET_NAME}_{FIELD_NAME} in UPPERCASE

# Example for secret "api_key" with field "value":
export API_KEY_VALUE="my-custom-value"

Solution:

# Correct format
export API_KEY_VALUE="my-value"
secretzero sync

# For template secrets
export DATABASE_CREDENTIALS_PASSWORD="my-password"
secretzero sync

docs.title: File Already Exists
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: File .env already exists (use merge: true to append)

Solution:

targets:
  - type: local-file
    path: .env
    format: dotenv
    merge: true  # ✅ Append/update instead of overwrite

docs.title: File Permission Denied
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Permission denied: '.env'

Solution:

# Check file permissions
ls -la .env

# Make writable
chmod u+w .env

# Or delete and regenerate
rm .env
secretzero sync

docs.title: Directory Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Directory 'config/secrets' does not exist

Solution:

SecretZero automatically creates parent directories. If this fails:

# Create directory manually
mkdir -p config/secrets

# Or check permissions on parent
ls -la config/

docs.title: AWS Secret Already Exists
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: ResourceExistsException: The secret /myapp/api_key already exists

Solution:

targets:
  - type: aws-secretsmanager
    name: /myapp/api_key
    # Option 1: Allow updates (recommended)
    update_existing: true

    # Option 2: Use different name
    # name: /myapp/api_key_v2

docs.title: Kubernetes Secret Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: secrets "app-secrets" not found in namespace "production"

Solution:

# Create namespace first
kubectl create namespace production

# Or use existing namespace
kubectl get namespaces

docs.title: Lockfile Corrupted
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Invalid lockfile format

Solution:

# Backup existing lockfile
cp .gitsecrets.lock .gitsecrets.lock.backup

# Delete and regenerate
rm .gitsecrets.lock
secretzero sync

docs.title: Hash Mismatch
docs.text:
Symptom:

Warning: Lockfile hash doesn't match current secret

Diagnosis:

# Check for drift
secretzero drift

# Check secret status
secretzero show api_key

Solution:

# Option 1: Resync to update lockfile
secretzero sync

# Option 2: Force regenerate
secretzero sync --force

docs.title: Lockfile Git Conflicts
docs.text:
Symptom:

<<<<<<< HEAD
  "api_key": {
    "hash": "sha256:abc123..."
=======
  "api_key": {
    "hash": "sha256:def456..."
>>>>>>> branch

Solution:

# Keep one version (usually newer)
git checkout --theirs .gitsecrets.lock

# Then resync to update
secretzero sync

docs.title: Rotation Not Due Yet
docs.text:
Symptom:

$ secretzero rotate
No secrets need rotation at this time.

Solution:

# Check rotation status
secretzero rotate --dry-run

# Force rotation if needed
secretzero rotate --force api_key

docs.title: One-Time Secret Can't Rotate
docs.text:
Symptom:

Warning: Secret 'master_key' is marked one_time, skipping rotation

Explanation:

This is expected behavior. One-time secrets are not rotated automatically.

Solution:

# To rotate anyway, remove from lockfile
secretzero sync --force master_key

# Or remove one_time flag

docs.title: Rotation Period Invalid
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Invalid rotation period '3 months'

Solution:

Use correct format:

# ❌ Invalid formats
rotation:
  period: "3 months"
  period: "90 days"

# ✅ Valid formats
rotation:
  period: 90d    # Days
  period: 12w    # Weeks
  period: 3m     # Months
  period: 1y     # Years

docs.title: Policy Validation Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Secret 'api_key' violates policy 'require_rotation'

Solution:

Add rotation period:

secrets:
  api_key:
    rotation:
      period: 90d  # ✅ Add rotation period

docs.title: SOC2 Compliance Failures
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Secret 'db_password' exceeds max age of 90 days

Solution:

secrets:
  db_password:
    rotation:
      period: 90d  # ✅ Must be ≤ 90 days for SOC2

docs.title: Access Policy Denials
docs.text:
Symptom:

Warning: Target 'local-file' is denied by policy 'cloud_only'

Solution:

# Option 1: Remove denied target
targets:
  - type: aws-secretsmanager  # ✅ Allowed

# Option 2: Update policy
policies:
  cloud_only:
    type: access
    config:
      allowed_targets:
        - aws-secretsmanager
        - local-file  # ✅ Add to allowed list

docs.title: API Server Won't Start
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: [Errno 98] Address already in use

Solution:

# Check what's using port 8000
lsof -i :8000

# Use different port
export SECRETZERO_PORT=9000
secretzero-api

docs.title: API Authentication Failed
docs.text:
Symptom:

$ curl http://localhost:8000/secrets
{"detail":"Missing API key"}

Solution:

# Set API key
export SECRETZERO_API_KEY="your-api-key"

# Include in request
curl -H "X-API-Key: $SECRETZERO_API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:8000/secrets

docs.title: API Returns 404
docs.text:
Symptom:

$ curl http://localhost:8000/api/secrets
{"detail":"Not Found"}

Solution:

Endpoints don't have /api prefix:

# ❌ Incorrect
curl http://localhost:8000/api/secrets

# ✅ Correct
curl http://localhost:8000/secrets

docs.title: GitHub Actions: Command Not Found
docs.text:
Symptom:

Run secretzero sync
secretzero: command not found

Solution:

Install SecretZero first:

steps:
  - name: Install SecretZero
    run: pip install secretzero[aws]

  - name: Sync Secrets
    run: secretzero sync

docs.title: GitLab CI: Authentication Failed
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: Unable to connect to AWS

Solution:

Add credentials as CI/CD variables:

sync-secrets:
  script:
    - pip install secretzero[aws]
    - secretzero sync
  variables:
    AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: $AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

docs.title: Jenkins: Pipeline Fails
docs.text:
Symptom:

Error: secretzero: not found

Solution:

pipeline {
  agent any
  stages {
    stage('Sync Secrets') {
      steps {
        sh '''
          python3 -m pip install secretzero[all]
          python3 -m secretzero sync
        '''
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Slow Secret Generation
docs.text:
Symptom:

Sync takes a long time to complete.

Diagnosis:

# Use dry-run to see what's slow
time secretzero sync --dry-run

Solutions:

  1. Script Generators: Check script execution time
  2. Cloud Targets: Check network latency
  3. Many Secrets: Consider batching

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text:
Symptom:

SecretZero using excessive memory.

Solutions:

  1. Reduce number of secrets per sync
  2. Split into multiple Secretfiles
  3. Use --force only when necessary

docs.title: Enable Debug Logging
docs.text:
# Set log level
export SECRETZERO_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG

# Run command
secretzero sync

docs.title: Collect Diagnostic Information

cat > diagnostic.txt << EOF
SecretZero Version: $(secretzero --version)
Python Version: $(python --version)
OS: $(uname -a)
Installed Packages: $(pip list | grep -E "(secretzero|boto3|azure|hvac)")
EOF
