docs.title: HashiCorp Vault Target
docs.text: SecretZero supports HashiCorp Vault KV (Key-Value) secret engines for secure secret storage. Vault provides a unified interface for secret management across hybrid cloud, multi-cloud, and on-premises environments with advanced features like dynamic secrets, encryption as a service, and comprehensive audit logging.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
HashiCorp Vault KV targets allow you to:

  • Store secrets in Vault's KV secret engines (v1 and v2)
  • Leverage Vault's encryption and security features
  • Integrate with multiple authentication methods (Token, AppRole, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure)
  • Enable secret versioning and rollback (KV v2)
  • Organize secrets hierarchically with custom mount points
  • Implement fine-grained access control with Vault policies
  • Audit all secret access with Vault's audit logging
  • Deploy in hybrid and multi-cloud environments
  • Use namespaces for multi-tenancy (Vault Enterprise)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
HashiCorp Vault support requires the HVAC (HashiCorp Vault API Client) library:

# Install with Vault support
pip install secretzero[vault]

# Or install hvac directly
pip install hvac

docs.title: Vault Server Setup
docs.text:
Ensure you have a Vault server running:

# Development server (not for production)
vault server -dev

# Production server requires configuration file
vault server -config=vault-config.hcl

For production deployments, see Vault deployment guide.

docs.title: Authentication Methods
docs.text: Vault supports multiple authentication methods. SecretZero integrates with the most common ones.

docs.title: Token Authentication
docs.text:
The simplest method, suitable for development and automation:

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      token: hvs.CAESID...  # Or use VAULT_TOKEN env var

Environment variables: 

export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com:8200
export VAULT_TOKEN=hvs.CAESID...


providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      # url and token read from environment

docs.title: AppRole Authentication
docs.text:
Recommended for machine-to-machine authentication:

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: approle
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role_id: 1234abcd-56ef-78gh-90ij-klmnopqrstuv
      secret_id: 9876zyxw-54vu-32ts-10rq-ponmlkjihgfe

Setup AppRole: 

# Enable AppRole auth
vault auth enable approle

# Create role
vault write auth/approle/role/secretzero \
  token_policies="secretzero-policy" \
  token_ttl=1h \
  token_max_ttl=4h

# Get role ID
vault read auth/approle/role/secretzero/role-id

# Generate secret ID
vault write -f auth/approle/role/secretzero/secret-id

docs.title: Kubernetes Authentication
docs.text:
For applications running in Kubernetes:

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: kubernetes
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role
      # JWT token read from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token

Setup Kubernetes auth: 

# Enable Kubernetes auth
vault auth enable kubernetes

# Configure Kubernetes auth
vault write auth/kubernetes/config \
  kubernetes_host=https://kubernetes.default.svc:443

# Create role
vault write auth/kubernetes/role/secretzero-role \
  bound_service_account_names=secretzero \
  bound_service_account_namespaces=default \
  policies=secretzero-policy \
  ttl=1h

docs.title: AWS IAM Authentication
docs.text:
For AWS environments using IAM credentials:

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: aws
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role
      # Uses AWS credentials from environment/instance profile

docs.title: Azure Authentication
docs.text:
For Azure environments using managed identities:

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: azure
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role
      # Uses Azure managed identity

docs.title: KV Secret Engines
docs.text: Vault provides two versions of the KV secret engine with different capabilities.

docs.title: KV Version 2 (Recommended)
docs.text:
KV v2 provides secret versioning, allowing you to track changes and roll back to previous versions.

Features: - Versioning - Every secret update creates a new version - Metadata - Track creation time, custom metadata - Soft delete - Deleted versions can be undeleted - Check-and-Set - Prevent concurrent updates - TTL - Set automatic secret expiration

Default mount: secret/

docs.title: KV Version 1 (Legacy)
docs.text:
KV v1 provides simple key-value storage without versioning.

Features: - Simple storage - Store and retrieve values - No versioning - Updates overwrite previous values - Lower overhead - Minimal metadata storage

Use cases: Simple environments, backwards compatibility

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
targets:
  - provider: vault
    kind: kv
    config:
      path: string          # Secret path (required)
      mount_point: string   # KV mount point (optional, default: "secret")
      version: integer      # KV version: 1 or 2 (optional, default: 2)

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text: Option Type Required Default Description path string Yes - Secret path in KV engine (e.g., "myapp/config") mount_point string No "secret" KV mount point path version integer No 2 KV engine version: 1 or 2

docs.title: Path Structure
docs.text:
KV v2 paths: 

# Store/update: mount_point/data/path
secret/data/myapp/config

# Retrieve: mount_point/data/path
secret/data/myapp/config

# Metadata: mount_point/metadata/path
secret/metadata/myapp/config

Note: SecretZero automatically handles the /data/ and /metadata/ prefixes for KV v2.

KV v1 paths: 

# All operations: mount_point/path
secret/myapp/config

docs.title: Basic KV v2 Storage
docs.text:
Store secrets in Vault using default KV v2 engine:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      token: hvs.CAESID...

secrets:
  - name: database_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
      special: true
      exclude_characters: '"@/\'
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/database/password
          mount_point: secret
          version: 2

docs.title: KV v1 Usage
docs.text:
Use KV v1 for simple storage without versioning:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200

secrets:
  - name: api_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 32
      charset: alphanumeric
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/api-key
          mount_point: kv-v1
          version: 1

Enable KV v1 engine: 

vault secrets enable -path=kv-v1 -version=1 kv

docs.title: Custom Mount Points
docs.text:
Use different mount points for organizational separation:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: approle
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role_id: ${VAULT_ROLE_ID}
      secret_id: ${VAULT_SECRET_ID}

secrets:
  # Application secrets
  - name: app_secret_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 64
      charset: base64
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: web/secret-key
          mount_point: applications

  # Infrastructure secrets
  - name: ssh_private_key
    kind: static
    config:
      value: |
        -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
        ...
        -----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: servers/prod/ssh-key
          mount_point: infrastructure

  # Database credentials
  - name: db_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: postgres/prod/password
          mount_point: databases

Setup custom mount points: 

vault secrets enable -path=applications kv-v2
vault secrets enable -path=infrastructure kv-v2
vault secrets enable -path=databases kv-v2

docs.title: Versioned Secrets
docs.text:
Leverage KV v2 versioning for change tracking:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200

secrets:
  - name: rotating_api_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/external-api/key
          version: 2

Access secret versions: 

# Get current version
vault kv get secret/services/external-api/key

# Get specific version
vault kv get -version=2 secret/services/external-api/key

# View version history
vault kv metadata get secret/services/external-api/key

# Rollback to previous version
vault kv rollback -version=2 secret/services/external-api/key

# Undelete a version
vault kv undelete -versions=3 secret/services/external-api/key

docs.title: Hierarchical Secret Organization
docs.text:
Organize secrets using path hierarchies:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200

secrets:
  # Production environment
  - name: prod_db_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/prod/database/password

  - name: prod_redis_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 24
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/prod/cache/redis/password

  - name: prod_api_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/prod/api/external-service/key

  # Staging environment
  - name: staging_db_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/staging/database/password

  - name: staging_api_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/staging/api/external-service/key

  # Shared secrets
  - name: shared_encryption_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 64
      charset: hex
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/shared/encryption/master-key

Path structure: 

secret/data/myapp/
├── prod/
│   ├── database/
│   │   └── password
│   ├── cache/
│   │   └── redis/
│   │       └── password
│   └── api/
│       └── external-service/
│           └── key
├── staging/
│   ├── database/
│   │   └── password
│   └── api/
│       └── external-service/
│           └── key
└── shared/
    └── encryption/
        └── master-key

docs.title: Multi-Environment with Namespaces
docs.text:
Use Vault Enterprise namespaces for multi-tenancy:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault_prod:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      token: ${VAULT_TOKEN_PROD}
      namespace: production  # Vault Enterprise feature

  vault_dev:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      token: ${VAULT_TOKEN_DEV}
      namespace: development

secrets:
  # Production namespace
  - name: prod_secret
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault_prod
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/database/password

  # Development namespace
  - name: dev_secret
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault_dev
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/database/password

Namespace hierarchy: 

/
├── production/
│   └── secret/data/myapp/database/password
└── development/
    └── secret/data/myapp/database/password

docs.title: Microservices Architecture
docs.text:
Organize secrets for microservices:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: kubernetes
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200
      role: microservices-role

secrets:
  # Shared service mesh certificates
  - name: service_mesh_ca
    kind: static
    config:
      value: |
        -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
        ...
        -----END CERTIFICATE-----
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: shared/service-mesh/ca-cert

  # Auth service
  - name: auth_db_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/auth/database/password

  - name: auth_jwt_secret
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 64
      charset: base64
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/auth/jwt/signing-key

  # Payment service
  - name: payment_stripe_key
    kind: static
    config:
      value: sk_live_...
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/payment/stripe/api-key

  - name: payment_db_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/payment/database/password

  # Notification service
  - name: notification_smtp_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 24
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/notification/smtp/password

  - name: notification_twilio_token
    kind: static
    config:
      value: ${TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN}
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: services/notification/twilio/auth-token

docs.title: Structured Secrets
docs.text:
Store complex credentials as structured data:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200

secrets:
  - name: database_credentials
    kind: templates.db_config

templates:
  db_config:
    fields:
      host:
        generator:
          kind: static
          config:
            default: postgres.example.com
      port:
        generator:
          kind: static
          config:
            default: "5432"
      database:
        generator:
          kind: static
          config:
            default: production
      username:
        generator:
          kind: static
          config:
            default: app_user
      password:
        generator:
          kind: random_password
          config:
            length: 32
            special: true
      ssl_mode:
        generator:
          kind: static
          config:
            default: require
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/database/config

Retrieved as: 

vault kv get secret/myapp/database/config


{
  "host": "postgres.example.com",
  "port": "5432",
  "database": "production",
  "username": "app_user",
  "password": "randompassword123456789012345678901",
  "ssl_mode": "require"
}

docs.title: Multi-Cloud Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy secrets across multiple cloud providers:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault_aws:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: aws
      url: https://vault-aws.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role

  vault_azure:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: azure
      url: https://vault-azure.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role

  vault_gcp:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: gcp
      url: https://vault-gcp.example.com:8200
      role: secretzero-role

secrets:
  # Global secrets replicated across clouds
  - name: global_api_key
    kind: random_string
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault_aws
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: global/api-key

      - provider: vault_azure
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: global/api-key

      - provider: vault_gcp
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: global/api-key

  # Cloud-specific secrets
  - name: aws_secrets
    kind: templates.aws_creds

  - name: azure_secrets
    kind: templates.azure_creds

  - name: gcp_secrets
    kind: templates.gcp_creds

docs.title: Differences Between KV v1 and KV v2
Feature Comparison
docs.text: Feature KV v1 KV v2 Versioning No Yes - automatic versioning Rollback No Yes - restore previous versions Soft Delete No Yes - deleted versions can be undeleted Metadata Limited Rich metadata with timestamps Check-and-Set No Yes - prevent concurrent updates API Path mount/path mount/data/path and mount/metadata/path Performance Faster (less overhead) Slightly slower (metadata storage) Storage Minimal overhead Higher overhead (versions + metadata)

docs.title: Migration from KV v1 to KV v2
docs.text:
1. Upgrade existing mount: 

# Check current version
vault secrets list -detailed

# Upgrade KV v1 to v2 (preserves data)
vault kv enable-versioning secret/

2. Update SecretZero configuration: 

# Before (KV v1)
config:
  path: myapp/secret
  version: 1

# After (KV v2)
config:
  path: myapp/secret
  version: 2

3. Verify migration: 

# Check secret versions
vault kv metadata get secret/myapp/secret

docs.title: Dynamic Secrets
docs.text:
Vault can generate dynamic credentials on-demand. While SecretZero focuses on static secrets, you can reference Vault's dynamic secrets:

# Enable database secrets engine
vault secrets enable database

# Configure PostgreSQL
vault write database/config/postgresql \
  plugin_name=postgresql-database-plugin \
  connection_url="postgresql://{{username}}:{{password}}@postgres:5432/mydb" \
  allowed_roles="app-role" \
  username="vault" \
  password="vault-password"

# Create role
vault write database/roles/app-role \
  db_name=postgresql \
  creation_statements="CREATE ROLE \"{{name}}\" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '{{password}}' VALID UNTIL '{{expiration}}';" \
  default_ttl="1h" \
  max_ttl="24h"

# Generate credentials (outside SecretZero)
vault read database/creds/app-role

docs.title: Encryption as a Service (Transit)
docs.text:
Use Vault's transit engine for encryption operations:

# Enable transit engine
vault secrets enable transit

# Create encryption key
vault write -f transit/keys/myapp

# Encrypt data
vault write transit/encrypt/myapp \
  plaintext=$(echo "sensitive data" | base64)

# Decrypt data
vault write transit/decrypt/myapp \
  ciphertext=vault:v1:8SDd3WHDOjf7mq69CyCqYjBXAiQQAVZRkFM13ok481zoCmHnSeDX9vyf7w==

docs.title: Secret Rotation
docs.text:
Implement secret rotation workflows:

version: '1.0'

providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200

secrets:
  - name: rotating_password
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/rotating/password
          version: 2  # Enables version history

Rotation workflow: 

# 1. SecretZero updates secret (creates new version)
secretzero sync

# 2. Application reads new version
vault kv get -version=2 secret/myapp/rotating/password

# 3. If needed, rollback to previous version
vault kv rollback -version=1 secret/myapp/rotating/password

# 4. View rotation history
vault kv metadata get secret/myapp/rotating/password

docs.title: Response Wrapping
docs.text:
Secure secret delivery using response wrapping:

# Wrap secret response (1-time use token)
vault kv get -wrap-ttl=5m secret/myapp/password

# Client unwraps with single-use token
vault unwrap <wrapping-token>

docs.title: 1. Secret Path Organization
docs.text:
Use consistent, hierarchical paths:

# Good: Clear hierarchy
secrets/
  myapp/
    prod/
      database/
        password
      api/
        key
    staging/
      database/
        password

# Avoid: Flat structure
secrets/
  myapp-prod-db-pass
  myapp-prod-api-key
  myapp-staging-db-pass

docs.title: 2. Use KV v2 for Production
docs.text:
Enable versioning for better change tracking and recovery:

config:
  version: 2  # Always use v2 for production

Benefits: - Roll back mistakes - Track change history - Implement check-and-set for safety - Enable secret rotation workflows

docs.title: 3. Implement Vault Policies
docs.text:
Create least-privilege policies:

# Application read-only policy
path "secret/data/myapp/prod/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}

# SecretZero write policy
path "secret/data/myapp/*" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete", "list"]
}

path "secret/metadata/myapp/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list", "delete"]
}

# Admin policy
path "secret/*" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete", "list"]
}

Apply policy: 

vault policy write secretzero-policy secretzero-policy.hcl
vault token create -policy=secretzero-policy

docs.title: 4. Enable Audit Logging
docs.text:
Monitor all secret access:

# Enable file audit device
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault/audit.log

# Enable syslog audit device
vault audit enable syslog tag="vault" facility="AUTH"

# View audit logs
tail -f /var/log/vault/audit.log | jq

Audit log example: 

{
  "time": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "type": "response",
  "auth": {
    "token_type": "service",
    "policies": ["default", "secretzero-policy"]
  },
  "request": {
    "operation": "read",
    "path": "secret/data/myapp/prod/database/password"
  },
  "response": {
    "data": {
      "data": {},
      "metadata": {
        "version": 3
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Use Namespaces for Multi-Tenancy
docs.text:
Isolate environments or teams (Vault Enterprise):

# Production namespace
providers:
  vault_prod:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      namespace: prod

# Development namespace
providers:
  vault_dev:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      namespace: dev

docs.title: 6. Implement Secret Versioning Strategy
docs.text:
Define version retention policies:

# Configure version retention
vault kv metadata put -max-versions=10 secret/myapp/password

# Configure check-and-set requirement
vault kv metadata put -cas-required=true secret/myapp/sensitive

# View metadata
vault kv metadata get secret/myapp/password

docs.title: 7. Use Token Policies
docs.text:
Create service-specific tokens:

# Short-lived token for CI/CD
vault token create \
  -policy=secretzero-policy \
  -ttl=1h \
  -use-limit=10

# Periodic token for services
vault token create \
  -policy=app-read-policy \
  -period=24h \
  -renewable

docs.title: 8. Secure Token Storage
docs.text:
Never commit tokens to version control:

# Use environment variables
providers:
  vault:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      kind: token
      url: ${VAULT_ADDR}
      token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}  # From environment

# Set in CI/CD
export VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.example.com:8200
export VAULT_TOKEN=hvs.CAESID...

# Or use auth methods without tokens
# AppRole, Kubernetes, AWS IAM, Azure, etc.

docs.title: 9. High Availability Setup
docs.text:
Deploy Vault with HA for production:

# vault-config.hcl
storage "raft" {
  path = "/vault/data"
  node_id = "node1"

  retry_join {
    leader_api_addr = "https://vault-1:8200"
  }
  retry_join {
    leader_api_addr = "https://vault-2:8200"
  }
}

listener "tcp" {
  address = "0.0.0.0:8200"
  tls_cert_file = "/vault/tls/cert.pem"
  tls_key_file = "/vault/tls/key.pem"
}

api_addr = "https://vault-node:8200"
cluster_addr = "https://vault-node:8201"
ui = true

docs.title: 10. Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
Implement backup and recovery:

# Take Raft snapshot
vault operator raft snapshot save backup.snap

# Restore from snapshot
vault operator raft snapshot restore backup.snap

# List snapshots
vault operator raft snapshot inspect backup.snap

docs.title: Connection Failures
docs.text:
Problem: VaultConnectionError or connection timeouts.

Solutions:

  1. Verify Vault server is running: 

    vault status

  2. Check network connectivity: 

    curl https://vault.example.com:8200/v1/sys/health

  3. Verify TLS certificates: 

    openssl s_client -connect vault.example.com:8200

  4. Check firewall rules: 

    telnet vault.example.com 8200

docs.title: Authentication Failures
docs.text:
Problem: VaultAuthError or permission denied.

Solutions:

  1. Verify token is valid: 

    vault token lookup

  2. Check token policies: 

    vault token lookup -format=json | jq .data.policies

  3. Test authentication: 

    # Token auth
vault login <token>

# AppRole auth
vault write auth/approle/login role_id=<role-id> secret_id=<secret-id>

  4. Verify auth method is enabled: 

    vault auth list

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
Problem: 403 permission denied when accessing secrets.

Solutions:

  1. Check policy permissions: 

    vault policy read secretzero-policy

  2. Verify path capabilities: 

    vault token capabilities secret/data/myapp/password

  3. Test access: 

    vault kv get secret/myapp/password

  4. Update policy if needed: 

    # Add required capabilities
path "secret/data/myapp/*" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete", "list"]
}

docs.title: Secret Not Found
docs.text:
Problem: 404 secret not found when retrieving secrets.

Solutions:

  1. Verify secret exists: 

    vault kv list secret/myapp

  2. Check path is correct: 

    # KV v2: Don't include /data/ in config path
# SecretZero handles this automatically

# Wrong:
path: secret/data/myapp/password

# Correct:
path: myapp/password
mount_point: secret

  3. Verify mount point: 

    vault secrets list

  4. Check secret version: 

    vault kv get -version=1 secret/myapp/password

docs.title: KV Version Mismatch
docs.text:
Problem: API errors due to incorrect KV version.

Solutions:

  1. Check KV version: 

    vault secrets list -detailed | grep secret

  2. Update configuration: 

    # Match KV version in Vault
config:
  path: myapp/password
  version: 2  # or 1

  3. Upgrade KV v1 to v2: 

    vault kv enable-versioning secret/

docs.title: Sealed Vault
docs.text:
Problem: Vault is sealed error.

Solutions:

  1. Check seal status: 

    vault status

  2. Unseal Vault: 

    vault operator unseal <unseal-key-1>
vault operator unseal <unseal-key-2>
vault operator unseal <unseal-key-3>

  3. Use auto-unseal (production): 

    # AWS KMS auto-unseal
seal "awskms" {
  region     = "us-east-1"
  kms_key_id = "alias/vault-unseal"
}

docs.title: HVAC Library Issues
docs.text:
Problem: ImportError: No module named 'hvac'.

Solution: 

pip install secretzero[vault]
# or
pip install hvac

docs.title: Encryption at Rest
docs.text:
Vault encrypts all data using AES-256-GCM:

# Storage backend configuration
storage "raft" {
  path = "/vault/data"
}

# All data encrypted with master key
# Master key protected by seal mechanism

docs.title: Encryption in Transit
docs.text:
Always use TLS for Vault communication:

listener "tcp" {
  address = "0.0.0.0:8200"
  tls_cert_file = "/vault/tls/cert.pem"
  tls_key_file = "/vault/tls/key.pem"
  tls_min_version = "tls12"
}

# Use HTTPS URLs
providers:
  vault:
    auth:
      url: https://vault.example.com:8200  # Not http://

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:
Implement fine-grained policies:

# Read-only access to specific paths
path "secret/data/myapp/prod/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}

# Write access to specific paths
path "secret/data/myapp/staging/*" {
  capabilities = ["create", "read", "update", "delete"]
}

# Deny access to sensitive paths
path "secret/data/admin/*" {
  capabilities = ["deny"]
}

docs.title: Token Security
docs.text:
Best practices:

  1. Use short TTLs: 

    vault token create -ttl=1h

  2. Implement token renewal: 

    vault token renew

  3. Use periodic tokens for services: 

    vault token create -period=24h

  4. Revoke unused tokens: 

    vault token revoke <token>

  5. Use token accessors for management: 

    vault list auth/token/accessors
vault token revoke -accessor <accessor>

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text:
Enable comprehensive audit logging:

# File-based audit log
vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault/audit.log

# Syslog audit log
vault audit enable syslog

# Socket audit log
vault audit enable socket address=127.0.0.1:9090 socket_type=tcp

Monitor audit logs: 

# Watch audit events
tail -f /var/log/vault/audit.log | jq 'select(.request.operation=="read")'

# Track failed authentication
tail -f /var/log/vault/audit.log | jq 'select(.error != null)'

docs.title: Secret Rotation
docs.text:
Implement regular rotation:

# Use KV v2 for version history
secrets:
  - name: rotated_secret
    kind: random_password
    config:
      length: 32
    targets:
      - provider: vault
        kind: kv
        config:
          path: myapp/rotating-secret
          version: 2

Rotation process: 

# 1. Generate new secret version
secretzero sync

# 2. Update applications to use new version
vault kv get -version=latest secret/myapp/rotating-secret

# 3. Verify applications are using new version
# 4. Delete old versions
vault kv delete -versions=1,2,3 secret/myapp/rotating-secret

# Or destroy permanently
vault kv destroy -versions=1,2,3 secret/myapp/rotating-secret

docs.title: Namespace Isolation
docs.text:
Use namespaces for multi-tenancy (Enterprise):

# Isolate production from development
providers:
  vault_prod:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      namespace: production

  vault_dev:
    kind: vault
    auth:
      namespace: development

docs.title: Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
Implement DR strategy:

  1. Regular backups: 

    # Automated snapshot
vault operator raft snapshot save /backups/vault-$(date +%Y%m%d).snap

  2. Test recovery: 

    # Test restore in separate environment
vault operator raft snapshot restore /backups/vault-20240115.snap

  3. Replication (Enterprise): 

    # Enable DR replication
vault write -f sys/replication/dr/primary/enable

# Generate secondary token
vault write sys/replication/dr/primary/secondary-token id=secondary1

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
Vault Agent Injector:

# pod-with-secrets.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: myapp
  annotations:
    vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
    vault.hashicorp.com/role: "myapp-role"
    vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-database: "secret/data/myapp/database"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: myapp
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: myapp:latest

Vault CSI Provider:

# secretproviderclass.yaml
apiVersion: secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1
kind: SecretProviderClass
metadata:
  name: vault-secrets
spec:
  provider: vault
  parameters:
    vaultAddress: "https://vault.example.com:8200"
    roleName: "myapp-role"
    objects: |
      - objectName: "database-password"
        secretPath: "secret/data/myapp/database"
        secretKey: "password"

docs.title: AWS Lambda
docs.text:
import hvac
import os

def lambda_handler(event, context):
    # Use AWS IAM auth
    client = hvac.Client(url=os.environ['VAULT_ADDR'])
    client.auth.aws.iam_login(
        role='lambda-role',
        use_token=True,
        region='us-east-1'
    )

    # Read secret
    secret = client.secrets.kv.v2.read_secret_version(
        path='myapp/database',
        mount_point='secret'
    )

    password = secret['data']['data']['password']
    return {'statusCode': 200}
